syllabus_uncertainty: The 2026 NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics textbook has a new eight-chapter structure. CBSE assessment mapping should be confirmed before production import.

The Class X Science curriculum identifies Periodic Classification, Heredity and Evolution, and certain electricity topics as formative/not assessed in the year-end examination; they remain represented with appropriate review status in downstream normalization.

content.title: Ohm’s Law
content.summary: Potential difference equals current multiplied by resistance for an ohmic conductor.
content.explanation: Potential difference equals current multiplied by resistance for an ohmic conductor.
content.when_to_use: Use to relate voltage, current and resistance.

example.question: A 4 Ω resistor carries 2 A. Find V.

content.title: Electric Power
content.summary: Power is the rate of electrical energy transfer.
content.explanation: Power is the rate of electrical energy transfer.
content.when_to_use: Use according to the quantities given.

example.question: A device uses 2 A at 10 V. Find its power.

content.title: Lens Formula
content.summary: Relates focal length, object distance and image distance for a spherical lens using the Cartesian sign convention.
content.explanation: Relates focal length, object distance and image distance for a spherical lens using the Cartesian sign convention.
content.when_to_use: Use for image formation by a spherical lens.
conditions: Use the Cartesian sign convention consistently.

example.question: If f = 10 cm and u = −20 cm, find v.

common_mistakes: Mixing mirror and lens sign conventions.

content.title: Mirror Formula
content.summary: Relates focal length, object distance and image distance for a spherical mirror.
content.explanation: Relates focal length, object distance and image distance for a spherical mirror.
content.when_to_use: Use for spherical mirrors with the Cartesian sign convention.

example.question: For a concave mirror, u = −20 cm and f = −10 cm. Find v.

common_mistakes: Using the lens formula for a mirror.

content.title: Electrical Energy
content.formula_plain: E = P t = V I t
content.summary: Electrical energy is power multiplied by time.
content.explanation: Electrical energy is power multiplied by time.
content.when_to_use: Use to calculate energy consumed over time.

example.question: A 100 W bulb works for 10 s. Find energy used.

common_mistakes: Using hours without converting when joules are required.
keywords: E = P t = V I t

content.summary: High-yield science revision note.

sections.heading: Key points
points: Balance equations by changing coefficients, not subscripts.
Recognise combination, decomposition, displacement and double displacement reactions.
Oxidation and reduction occur together in redox reactions.

content.title: Life Processes
content.summary: High-yield science revision note.

sections.heading: Key points
points: Nutrition, respiration, transport and excretion maintain life.
Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy.
Different organisms use specialised organs and tissues for life processes.
